scope: Verifier diagnostic only; inherited Node TCP/IPC preload claims. No product acceptance or global PASS.
reviewMethod: static review plus one bounded private synthetic local TCP/IPC runtime probe

V01.finding: All 27 input bytes remain identical. R1 and R2 record zero source changes and matching source snapshot digests; full 1042-file inventories and 81 bindings are absent, so historical source freeze is corroborated by supplied records, not independently rehashed. Neither run is globally passing.

V02.finding: Real focused pinned HTTP tests and private ordinary TCP/IPC controls work, but mixed path+port options bypass IPC ownership. Guard selects TCP validation when port is present, then forwards path to Node, which connects IPC. Honest next-tick blocked errors exist for ordinary rejected paths; the mixed path is not rejected.

V03.finding: Five real focused files directly record 27 passed/1 failed. Qualification programs define positives and negatives and both command records report qualificationExit=0, but original qualification raw streams/registries are not among the 27 inputs. The private probe adds actual local positives and a negative plus a counterexample; it does not validate all resolution or inherited-child cases. Existing controls miss mixed path+port.

V04.finding: Classifications are supported by raw per-test observations, preserving uncertainty: transport false denials, worker exit-code transitions, and a retained closed-port policy mismatch. Other R1 failures remain unresolved. No totals are subtracted to infer global success and ECONNREFUSED is never fabricated.

strongestMaterialVerifierDefect.title: TCP authorization can be used to connect an unregistered IPC path
strongestMaterialVerifierDefect.expected: Asynchronous CVG_GLOBAL_TEST_NETWORK_BLOCKED for unowned IPC before connecting.
strongestMaterialVerifierDefect.observed: Path-only negative denied; identical path with owned TCP tuple connected and received UNREGISTERED_PRIVATE_IPC. Exactly one private IPC accept, and TCP accept count stayed at one from its positive control.
strongestMaterialVerifierDefect.remediation: Make authorization follow actual Node transport selection; validate IPC ownership whenever Node will use path, or reject ambiguous path+port options. Add an independent mixed-options negative control without rewriting the product smoke expectation or fabricating ECONNREFUSED. Re-review only the bounded guard change and affected evidence.

uncertainty: Only the manifest and 27 listed packet inputs were consulted; no repository history, AGENTS, ledgers, rationale outside those inputs, network documentation or external sources were read.
No original project test was rerun. Review combines static inspection and one private synthetic Node v22.23.2 probe, not a global runtime certification.

Probe uses a byte-identical relocated R2 guard loaded via require after creating a private IPC stand-in that is deliberately absent from its registry. This demonstrates the installed wrapper defect, not startup inheritance or a real third-party endpoint.

Original qualification stdout/stderr and qualification network/blocked logs, source-before/after inventories, candidate bindings, imported worker implementations and smoke implementation are outside the packet. qualificationExit and freeze claims remain supplied-run metadata.

Worker R1 exit 0 versus R2 exit 1 is observed by original assertions. Synchronous versus asynchronous guard behavior is a plausible mechanism, but child raw output and complete worker paths are missing, so exact mechanism is not proven.

TCP/IPC preload scope only. No OS sandbox, UDP, native-child, noninheriting Node, adversarial registry integrity or product acceptance attestation. IPv6/TLS, listener races and every connect signature were not exhaustively tested.
Remaining R1 boundary/manifest/dependency/fence failures were not rerun in R2 and cannot be reclassified as resolved. Skipped tests remain skipped.
